guards: every relative markdown link inside SYNCED content resolves, at that file's consumer path, to another path the sync also ships

poisonPill.why: A relative href is resolved against the directory its file sits in, and the sync moves files between directories at different depths — so a link an author verified by clicking it can be dead in every consumer. Two shapes, both measured 2026-09-04. Arithmetic: skills/<skill>/references/x.md is copied to .claude/skills/<skill>/references/x.md, one level deeper, so a ../../../docs/… written to reach the repo root from the first lands in .claude/ from the second; 47 links were dead this way, in the generated copies here and in every consumer. Structural: the closure ships exactly ONE docs/ file, so a ../plans/… from it cannot resolve there at any depth — that one was reported by wine-cellar-app (upstream 15da01b6) and cost them a permanent .sync-overrides.json entry, because hand-rewriting the line marked the whole document diverged and froze it off every future upstream change. Neither of the two existing gates could see any of it: check-docs-refs.mjs and check-skill-consumer-refs.mjs both extract literal docs/…md TOKENS, so a link whose TEXT says docs/plans/<name>.md and whose HREF says ../completed/x.md reads as healthy to both. The pill restores the reported line verbatim — the shape that already survived one href repair and two gates — and the gate must refuse it. The fixture also carries a fenced sample link, which must stay invisible: /ai-context-management ships three, showing a reader what to write into their own root AGENTS.md where ./AGENTS.md is the correct href, so a gate that rewrote or flagged those would corrupt a template.
